Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute headache for 3 days, described as on-going with fluctuations, primarily around the right eye but felt all over the head.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began about 3 days ago; gradually worsened; present at times at a high intensity.
- Severity: Pain rated around 8/10.
- Quality: Usually dull with occasional sharp pains.
- Aggravating/relieving factors: Worked at a computer; brightness/screen triggering symptoms; tried ibuprofen with limited relief over 2 days (patient reports taking three tablets per day).
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light sensitivity) and eye discomfort with bright lights; nausea without vomiting; neck stiffness; difficulty focusing but no speech difficulty or weakness; no vision loss reported.
- Analgesics at home: Ibuprofen used (dose not documented); reported no meaningful relief.
- Constancy/character: Headache present most of the time with intermittent intensity spikes.
- Past medical history: Headache history; not a known migraine patient; family history of migraines (mother and sister).
- Allergies: Allergies to medications not known.
- Medications: Regular medications none; no ongoing prescriptions.
- Social history: Smokes socially; drinks socially; works in IT; relies on computer screens; wears glasses; lives with three housemates; reports work-related stress due to a new project.
- Eye history: Wears glasses since age 5; not had an eye test recently.
- Review of systems: No fever, rash, or vomiting; no vision loss or weakness; neck stiffness noted.

Objective:
- No objective physical examination findings or vitals documented in the transcript.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Headache with migrainous features (probable migraine)
   - Assessment: Migraine-type headache favored by photophobia, unilateral/right-ocular emphasis, nausea, family history of migraines; however, the patient has not had a diagnosed migraine previously.
   - Differential diagnosis: Migraine; tension-type headache; other secondary headaches (not ruled out without examination).
   - Investigations planned: Headache diary to identify triggers; consider formal eye exam if symptoms persist or worsen.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Optimize analgesia: discuss increasing NSAID use and/or alternative analgesics.
       - Ibuprofen: patient has been taking three tablets per day; plan to maximize/adjust dosing to up to two tablets per dose, up to three times daily (dose/frequency not previously documented in detail).
       - Consider additional/alternative options: Naproxen; Paracetamol; Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Headache diary to identify triggers (environment, hydration, sleep, screen brightness, stress).
     - Follow-up: schedule a return visit in 1–2 weeks; sooner if headaches worsen or new red flags develop.
     - Prophylaxis consideration: If headaches become more frequent, discuss prophylactic medication at the next visit.
   - Referrals: None at this time; no imaging or specialist referral discussed.

Quality checks (document quality):
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No documented vitals or bedside exam; no imaging or labs ordered; no explicit allergy/medication reconciliation beyond patient report; no explicit ophthalmology referral unless symptoms persist.
- Internal conflicts: None clearly identified in the transcript (no contradictory statements about neck stiffness aside from minor dialogue flow).
- Transcript quality: Some repetition and minor conversational noise; overall understandable. No major inaudible sections identified.

Note: All medication references include the caveat that dose/route/frequency were not fully documented for some items.
